evidence.ai_role: Learned object detection classifies pollen states and tube tips, enabling time-resolved phenotyping across the accession panel.
evidence.tested: New in-vitro pollen time courses with at least 7 usable replicates per condition/accession; learned counts checked against manual annotations.
evidence.unknown: Confidence-threshold selection used count agreement; model accuracy may be optimistic. Image exclusions and varying replicate counts limit transfer. No field fertility, yield or causal genetic benefit established.

organization: University of Arizona; Ohio State University

source_review.scope: Primary full manuscript Methods, Results, validation protocol and limitations independently reviewed.

summary: A preprint fine-tuned CenterNet HourGlass104 to count and track pollen in approximately 300,000 time-lapse images from 218 tomato accessions and wild relatives. In vitro, raising temperature from 26°C to 34°C increased mean bursting at two hours from 14.9% to 83.1%, while tube-length responses varied: 72% of accessions had shorter tubes and 28% had equal or greater length. Manual-count agreement supported image measurements. These are controlled pollen-assay phenotypes, not demonstrated field fertility or yield benefits; genotype effects and assay generalization need further testing.
title: Computer vision measures diverse tomato pollen responses to heat
